newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A crisis in the ruling party PASOK erupted yesterday following party secretary Costas Skandalidis's comments about "the prime ministerial circle". His comments drew fire from Prime Minister Costas Simitis himself. Reports say the quarrel is the tip of the iceberg and presages a wider internal party dispute.

--Ministers and party leaders yesterday gave a political flavour to the freak storms and destructive flash flooding which hit the country on Sunday, trading barbs over "who was to blame" for the damage.
--Washington yesterday called on Athens, Ankara and Nicosia to show "self-restraint" in action and word, following Nicosia's decision to not speed up procedures to deploy Russian S-300 missiles.
--The practice of surprise audits by the Athens bourse's supervising committee on all members has been recommended by the three international houses which recently audited all members.

--Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos insisted yesterday on his opposition to a moratorium on overflights over Cyprus as the government passes the ball to Ankara through US State Department official Carey Cavanaugh. Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said after talks with Cavanaugh that the Greek-Cyprus joint defence pact was not up for negotiation but that the government was prepared to take measures to reduce tension with Turkey.
--Simitis criticised Skandalidis for his comments yesterday but also tried to put an end to the issue.
--Ships remained at anchor for the second day yesterday while airports are expected to see problems over the weekend. Teachers and others will take labour action next week.

--Problems continue to plague various drenched regions around Greece while Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis orders an investigation into what's happening on Kifissos Avenue.
--Forty villages remain cut off in the Fthiotida region, with bridges down, roads unpassable and electricity and phone links cut.
--Conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert says the government's emergency assistance to victims of Sunday's floods is "a joke".
--Farmers are planning a new form of roadside protest which will allow vehicles to pass without paying tolls.

--The environment, town planning and public works ministry will examine how to avert flooding of Athens western suburbs every time the Kifissos river overflows at its meeting today. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
